Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

As a Technical Quality Specialist on the Customer Support team, you’ll play a critical role in shaping how Figma identifies, diagnoses, and resolves complex product issues at scale. As a founding member of our Bangalore team, you’ll help establish quality standards, influence workflows, and build strong partnerships with Engineering and Product.

We are looking for a Technical Quality Specialist who will drive quality improvements across the support and product lifecycle. This role goes beyond resolving issues—you’ll identify patterns, lead root cause analysis, and partner with Engineering and Product to improve reliability and customer experience at scale. The ideal candidate brings strong technical depth, systems thinking, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

Coverage outside standard business hours is part of this role. Your shift hours will be one of the following:

  • Wednesday to Sunday, 12.30pm - 9.30pm IST
  • Thursday to Monday, 12.30pm - 9.30pm IST
  • Friday to Tuesday, 12.30pm - 9.30pm IST

This role will be held from our Bengaluru office (in Koramangala) on a hybrid basis.

What you’ll do at Figma:

  • Develop deep expertise in Figma’s products, architecture, and customer workflows to diagnose complex technical issues
  • Interact with Figma customers daily via support channels such as chat, email, or video calls, taking ownership over complex problems
  • Own end-to-end resolution of high-impact bugs, partnering closely with Engineering and Product to drive timely and effective fixes, and maintain clear, proactive communication to improve customer satisfaction
  • Contribute to social support efforts by engaging with customers and users on social media and community platforms
  • Adapt to supporting customers across multiple products, including assisting with billing and account management issues as needed. Maintain schedule flexibility, including occasional weekend or holiday coverage, to support customers globally
  • Recommend and implement improvements to debugging workflows, tooling, and support operations
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to create internal documentation, training materials, and scalable knowledge systems
  • Act as the voice of the customer by identifying trends and communicating insights to our Product and Engineering teams to advocate for bug fixes, tooling and process improvements, and feature enhancements

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • 2+ years of experience in Technical Support, Support Engineering, or QA within a SaaS environment
  • Strong troubleshooting and debugging skills across Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, including REST APIs, OAuth authentication flows, and third-party integrations
  • Working knowledge of modern web technologies, including JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, CSS, and React
  • Ability to collaborate with Engineering and Product teams to resolve complex technical issues, with strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills
  • Comfortable navigating fast-paced, ambiguous environments, with a focus on end-to-end issue resolution and continuous process improvement

While not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

  • Experience working with design tools like Figma, Adobe Suite, Sketch, Framer

At Figma, one of our values is Grow as you go. We believe in hiring smart, curious people who are excited to learn and develop their skills. If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with the points outlined in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

About Commvault

Commvault (NASDAQ: CVLT) delivers continuous recovery for the AI era. We help organizations stay ready for constant disruption by returning critical data, applications, identities, and AI systems to a clean, trusted state. Our purpose-built recovery solutions span cloud-native and hybrid environments, leveraging AI to enable resilience at enterprise scale.

The Opportunity:

We have an exciting opportunity to join our Business Technology team. As we move toward an AI-driven delivery model, you will design and build end-to-end workflows that orchestrate ServiceNow, cloud platforms, enterprise systems, and AI agents into autonomous flows that resolve requests from intake through completion.

The ideal candidate starts with business outcomes and economics—understanding current costs and cycle times, defining target states, and designing the fastest path to achieve them. You will re-engineer processes before automating, determine what can be resolved autonomously versus requiring human intervention, and build the integrations that bring these solutions into production.

What you’ll do…

  • Orchestrate cross-platform workflows connecting ServiceNow, cloud services, identity systems, and enterprise applications to enable end-to-end request resolution without manual handoffs

  • Build AI-powered request resolution and autonomous operations (intent detection, diagnosis, and resolution), driving deflection before tickets are created

  • Integrate AI agents into workflows using MCP, tools, and orchestration patterns to pull context, take action, and escalate appropriately

  • Re-engineer processes before automating—eliminating unnecessary steps and designing improved workflows

  • Own automation economics and value realization, including measuring cost and cycle time, modeling improvements, and tracking business impact

  • Build and configure solutions on ServiceNow (Flow Designer, Integration Hub, scoped apps, catalog, Now Assist) alongside automation beyond the platform

  • Develop automation outside of ServiceNow using Python and PowerShell for cloud operations, identity management, monitoring, and scheduling

  • Design workflows that balance automation and human oversight—defining approval points, autonomy boundaries, and ensuring systems operate reliably and safely in production 

Who you are?

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field

  • 2–4 years of hands-on experience in software engineering, automation, or ServiceNow development, building production-grade solutions

  • Hands-on experience with ServiceNow development, including workflow automation (Flow Designer), integrations (REST/webhooks), and platform scripting

  • Experience working with authentication (OAuth, bearer tokens) and enterprise data models (e.g., CMDB)

  • Strong automation mindset with the ability to identify what should be orchestrated, automated, or eliminated

  • Solid engineering fundamentals (APIs, system design, data structures, scripting)

  • Experience with programming or scripting languages such as Python, Java, C#, or PowerShell

  • Experience building and integrating systems using REST APIs and enterprise platforms

  • Experience delivering end-to-end automation (design, build, deploy, monitor, measure)

  • Ability to work backward from business outcomes, with a focus on impact and efficiency

  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to operate in ambiguity and communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders

  • Demonstrated self-learning mindset in a rapidly evolving technology landscape

  • Curiosity to understand root causes—building solutions that address patterns, not just symptoms

  • Strong written and verbal English 

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Experience across additional ServiceNow modules (ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, CSM, SecOps, GRC)

  • Familiarity with ServiceNow capabilities such as Service Portal, UI Builder, Performance Analytics, Now Assist, or Virtual Agent

  • Experience building scoped applications (App Engine) and using automated testing frameworks (ATF)

  • Experience applying AI to workflow automation (e.g., request deflection, automated resolution, intent classification at scale)

  • Exposure to agent-based systems or orchestration patterns (e.g., MCP, tool integration, agent handoffs)

  • Familiarity with human-in-the-loop design, guardrails, and workflow governance

  • Experience with modern AI and integration frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, RAG pipelines)

  • Familiarity with vector databases, observability tooling, monitoring, or process mining

  • Experience with integration platforms (e.g., Workato, MuleSoft)

The Polaris Platform Bangalore team (a.k.a. Legion team) at Rubrik provides the core platforms and systems that enable product engineers to efficiently build and operate scalable and reliable applications in the cloud and also the on-prem version of the control plane. Polaris Platform has a horizontal charter with our customers being both external customers as well as Rubrik internal teams. Presently, the Legion team is working on enabling product led trials, license management & enforcement, making  its cloud deployment infrastructure more efficient. Legion team also owns the on-prem RSC (RSC-P) version and is currently working on supporting it on different deployments, while ensuring it scales and is performant like its cloud counterpart.

To do that, we have a very fluid structure and give people flexibility to work on projects that they enjoy the most. jobs.description:
About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Database Reliability Engineer to own the reliability, performance, and scalability of our end-to-end database infrastructure. You will manage both our low-latency transactional engines and our real-time analytical/lakehouse storage systems. You will bridge systems engineering, database internals, and automation to maintain rock-solid data integrity, low query latency, and high availability across the entire data lifecycle.

What you'll do

  • Performance & Query Optimization: Diagnose and resolve latency regressions, lock/latch contention, index strategies, and memory/disk bottlenecks across both row-oriented and columnar engines.
  • Disaster Recovery & Data Integrity: Ensure strict RTO/RPO adherence, automated backup validation, PITR (point-in-time recovery), and data consistency across transactional and analytical stores.
  • Storage Optimization & Compaction: Manage compaction policies, partition strategies, file sizing, and storage tiering to minimize storage costs and read amplification.
  • Transactional Reliability & Operations: Manage HA, automated failover, replication topology, and zero-downtime maintenance for production RDBMS clusters.
  • Analytical Storage Infrastructure: Maintain, scale, and optimize real-time analytical engines (ClickHouse) and lakehouse formats/engines (Apache Iceberg, BigQuery).
  • Infrastructure as Code & Observability: Build declarative automation for cluster provisioning, schema migrations, and metric alerting (Prometheus, PromQL, Grafana)

Experience you'll need

  • Database Internals & RDBMS Fundamentals:
    • Deep understanding of ACID guarantees, WAL, checkpointing, and recovery mechanics (e.g., ARIES-style recovery).
    • Comprehensive grasp of concurrency control, transaction isolation levels, lock protocols (2PL, deadlocks), and MVCC architectures.
    • Deep knowledge of storage structures: B+ Trees, LSM-Trees, and columnar storage layouts (e.g., Parquet, ORC, ClickHouse Wide/Compact formats).
  • Operational Database Experience:
    • 4+ years running production database infrastructure, with deep expertise in [PostgreSQL / MySQL].
    • Experience optimizing and managing cost/quotas in Google Cloud BigQuery (partitioning, clustering, reservation slots).
    • Experience with OLAP DB like: ClickHouse, BQ
  • Systems & Kernel Engineering:
    • Strong Linux fundamentals: I/O subsystems, page cache vs. engine buffer pools, disk alignment, asynchronous I/O, and memory management.
    • Automation & Software Engineering:

About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 

Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

Your role

Stripe is large enough that individual products and projects can be rapidly deployed to a meaningful fraction of the world’s businesses, but small enough that individual agency still has outsized impact. Small teams can impact how millions of businesses grow. Right now the global economy is replatforming around AI, creating new opportunities for growth. We’re at the center of this, and we think the best work is still in front of us.

To meet this moment, we’re looking for people who move with urgency, like hard problems, and want their work to matter at a time of great change. If that’s you, there’s no better place to build your career.

Who you are

  • Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.

  • Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before. 

  • Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities.  At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.

Minimum requirements

  • A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science or a directly related field, obtained by summer 2027, or equivalent work experience; New grad candidates should have no more than 18 months of professional experience (excluding internship experience).

  • Experience and familiarity with programming, either through side projects or classwork. We work mostly in Java, Ruby, JavaScript, Scala, and Go. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present.

  • Experience from either previous internships or working collaboratively on multi-person coding projects (in a university or professional setting).

  • Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor or subject matter experts.

  • Clear written communication skills, with the ability to explain your work to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes.

  • Ability to leverage AI tools to accelerate development while applying rigorous critical thinking and professional judgement to review, refine, and validate all outputs.

Preferred qualifications

  • One or more areas of specialized knowledge (frontend, backend, infrastructure or other technologies) balanced with general skills and knowledge.

  • Familiarity with navigating and managing work in large code bases.

  • Experience leading small projects independently, and contributing to larger projects alongside peers.

  • Ability to operate with high agency in navigating complex technical obstacles independently, knowing precisely when to unblock oneself and when to ask for help.

Rubrik secures and accelerates the world’s AI transformation. They learn from our data, act through our own agents, and improve with every decision. Fully backed by executive leadership, this team drives meaningful, large-scale enterprise transformation.

 

About the role

We want senior engineers who have already shipped agents that real people rely on, and who are ready to do it again at higher stakes. You will drop into the real work, redesign it around agents that carry it end to end, and ship it as the new way that part of Rubrik operates.You’ll own your agent systems end to end: understanding the workflow, designing the architecture, writing the code, deploying, and running it in production. Rather than simply querying an API, you engineer robust, production-grade infrastructure around model endpoints, integrating custom tooling, context pipelines, automated evaluations, and defensive guardrails to ensure resilience against unstructured real-world data. 

You also decide whether a problem needs an agent, a simpler automation, or nothing at all, and you have explicit authority to stop or re-scope work that won’t deliver impact. You thrive in ambiguous environments with a low-ego mindset, leveraging AI coding tools as core collaborative partners in your engineering workflow.

 

What you’ll do

  • Lead product discovery alongside Product Managers and domain experts to understand real workflows, map them out, and define clear problems, baselines, and success criteria as the foundation for building agentic solutions.
  • Design, build, test, and deploy production agents, automations, and internal tools using coding agents, LLM APIs, and agent frameworks, integrated with Rubrik’s internal agent platform and business systems.
  • Turn complex processes into multi-agent workflows that carry real work and make decisions: orchestrators that qualify and routes deals, workers that move orders through approval and fulfillment under business rules, agents that monitor signals and recommend actions for customer health, or coordinated agents that handle hire-to-retire steps across HR, IT, and managers with shared state and clear handoffs.
  • Engineer agents for autonomy with reliability, including tool and orchestration flows, context management, caching, retries, and failure handling.
  • Leverage full-stack engineering across backend services, APIs, data models, interactive screens, approval UIs, and chat interfaces as the complete medium to deliver high-ownership, user-facing agent systems.
  • Apply solid software engineering practices to AI systems, treating prompts, skills, configs, and specs as versioned artifacts, with code review, tests, CI or CD, and staged rollouts.
  • Implement evaluation, guardrails, and quality control: derive evals from workflow data, establish quality gates and guardrails, integrate human-in-the-loop approvals where needed, and monitor production runs to refine agents over time.
  • Use measured results to decide how to evolve or retire agents, and turn successful systems into patterns and libraries that can be reused.

Experience you’ll need (must haves)

  • Around 7 or more years of professional software engineering experience in production systems, and around 2 or more years of professional, hands-on experience building AI agents and agent powered production applications with measurable outcomes.
  • Strong full stack engineering background, with a track record of designing, building, and owning services end to end, including backend APIs and integrations, data models, and user facing interfaces such as approval UIs, dashboards, or chat surfaces.
  • A builder mindset: comfortable defining baselines and metrics, reporting results in business terms, working in a fast moving environment, and closing the loop by building, demoing, learning, and building again. If you like seeing improvements in hours saved, errors avoided, and teams unblocked, you will have plenty of chances to measure that here.

Software engineering skills and best practices

  • System design: break down complex problems, design APIs and data models, reason about latency, throughput, and failure modes, and choose simple, robust architectures.
  • Algorithms, data structures, access control permissions, and data provenance.
  • Spec driven development: turn vague requirements into clear problem statements, write or refine design docs, and use a Spec → Plan → Task → Code→ Converge flow so work is traceable from design to code, including when you use AI coding agents.
  • Execution discipline: use version control, code review, automated tests, CI or CD, staged rollouts and rollbacks, logging, metrics, and tracing, and improve systems based on issues and signals from production.

AI engineering skills and best practices

  • Build agents in code using LLM APIs, SDKs, and libraries, not just no code or low code tools, and have shipped agentic systems that real users rely on.
  • Design robust agent harnesses and multi agent orchestrations: model tools and resources, manage context and state, and keep runs reliable under real world data and load.
  • Establish continuous evaluation and safety mechanisms: turn production failures into test cases, gate changes on eval suite results, and enforce guardrails across agent workflows.
  • Exercise clear judgment on AI fit: decide when a problem needs an agent versus a simpler automation or no build, and make tradeoffs around model choice, latency and cost, context strategy, and autonomy using data rather than intuition.

Preferred qualifications (nice to haves)

  • Knowledge/context graphs: entities and relationships, GraphRAG, hybrid retrieval.
  • Agent frameworks and runtimes: Google ADK, LangGraph, OpenAI style, cloud or container platforms.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI or similar stacks.
  • Tools integration: MCP, Slack or Teams bots, REST APIs, webhooks.
  • Data systems: Snowflake, Salesforce, graph stores.
  • UX: conversational flows, chat surfaces, guided forms, simple dashboards for agent output.
